facts.value: ferrite magnets had largely displaced alnico in small motors and magnetic separators; the modern Nd-Fe-B magnets did not arrive until the 1980s

children.note: Nd-Fe-B magnets were commercialised around 1982-84, so an 1982 separator would be ferrite or alnico, not Nd-Fe-B. Medium-high confidence.

metal.manganese.furnace-lining.name: The submerged arc furnace and its refractory
metal.manganese.furnace-lining.description: A ferromanganese furnace is 25-100 MVA with three electrodes 1.5-2.0 m in diameter, and the difference from a silicon furnace is the slag: the ferromanganese process makes a large volume of a liquid, low-basicity slag, so the furnace is a slag vessel with an electrode in it. The shell is steel with a refractory lining of magnesite or magnesite-carbon, and the lining is eroded by the slag at 1500 C faster than in a silicon furnace. Carbon pastes, electrode paste made of the same coke-and-pitch as the aluminium anode, are rammed into holes in the roof around each electrode. So a ferromanganese plant is a coke-and-pitch shop as much as a manganese shop, which is the same convergence as the ferrochrome and ferrosilicon branches.

facts.label: Furnace
facts.value: 25-100 MVA, three electrodes 1.5-2.0 m diameter, 1400-1600 C

facts.label: Lining
facts.value: magnesite or magnesite-carbon, eroded by the low-basicity slag

facts.label: Electrode paste
facts.value: rammed into roof holes, made of coke and pitch

metal.manganese.furnace-lining.note: Medium confidence; the ferromanganese furnace design is well described in ferroalloy practice.

metal.aluminum.cold-rolling.name: Cold rolling on a Sendimir high-roll mill
metal.aluminum.cold-rolling.description: The 2-6 mm hot strip goes to a multi-high cold mill - a Sendimir 20-high or 24-high arrangement where a small work roll is backed by many intermediate rolls, giving the enormous rolling force needed at a small gap without a mill body the size of a building. The work rolls are hardened tool steel, 100-300 mm diameter, with a chasing finish that the operator keeps polished with emery and a lint-free cloth while the mill runs; at 6 um a single fingerprint is a visible defect. Between passes the strip is annealed at 200-400 C in a gas-fired or electric furnace, because the roll gap cannot take the whole reduction in one pass and because that anneal is what resets the rolling texture. The finished 1-2 t coil, 400-1300 mm wide, is then slit into customer widths with tungsten-carbide or ceramic-coated knives and re-spooled, which is the least forgiving part of the whole operation: at 6 um the foil has almost no stiffness and simply tears on a blunt knife. From 1980 onwards the Sendimir Z-High mill, which adds separate work-roll bending and flattening control, was the state of the art for aluminium foil width.

facts.label: Mill configuration
facts.value: 20-high or 24-high Sendimir; the Sendimir Z-High from 1980

facts.label: Work roll diameter
facts.value: 100-300 mm, tool steel, changed frequently

facts.label: Reduction
facts.value: about 40-70% per pass, 15-30 um per pass to foil

facts.label: Gauge control
facts.value: hydraulic or electromechanical gap and bending control to about 1-2% thickness tolerance

facts.label: Interstage anneal
facts.value: 200-400 C, batch or inline; also where the rolling-direction texture is set

facts.label: Slitting
facts.value: a 1-2 t coil of 400-1300 mm slit to 100-600 mm on carbide or ceramic-coated knives

metal.hematite.stockyard.name: The ore stockyard and the ship loader
metal.hematite.stockyard.description: Because the ships are 180,000-250,000 dwt and the mine's output is lumpy, the ore goes into a 1-2 million tonne stockyard with a stacker and a travelling shiploader. The shiploader is a 100 m long gantry on rails with a slewing chute that trims the ship's hold as it loads, so a 250,000 dwt vessel is filled flat without a bulker or a trimming machine. The whole Pilbara export chain - mine, conveyor, stockyard, loader, ship - was built to move one commodity in enormous tonnage at very low cost, and it is the reason Australian iron ore is the cheapest iron in the world.

facts.label: Stockyard
facts.value: 1-2 Mt live capacity, stacker and a travelling tripper

facts.label: Shiploader
facts.value: travelling, slewing, with a trimming chute

facts.label: Loading rate
facts.value: 1,500-10,000 t per hour

facts.label: Vessel
facts.value: 180,000-250,000 dwt capesize, loaded in 12-24 h

The Pilbara reference gives the region's resource and production rate but no port or stockyard engineering, and the neighbouring ore-loader node carries the ship figures instead.

metal.dielectric-grading.name: Grade the barium titanate powder into a dielectric class
metal.dielectric-grading.description: The same powder cannot make a Y5V capacitor and an X7R one. Y5V is made from a fine, uniform, high-surface-area powder near the Curie point, where the dielectric constant is enormous and wildly temperature-dependent - a huge capacitance that changes by a factor of five over the working range. X7R is made from a coarser powder with barium zirconate or barium strontium titanate added, which flattens the temperature curve at the cost of the peak. So the capacitor 'class' is really a powder specification, and the class marking on the part is a statement about the ball mill that ground it.

facts.label: Y5V
facts.value: fine powder near the Curie point, K of several thousand, very high temperature coefficient

facts.label: X7R
facts.value: coarser powder with solid solution, K of 1000-4000, +/-15% over -55 to +125 C

facts.label: Additives
facts.value: Ba(Zr,Ti)O3, Ba(Sr,Ti)O3, and rare-earth dopants for the high-capacitance grades

metal.dielectric-grading.note: Medium confidence; the class-to-chemistry mapping is standard and the recipes are proprietary.

children.name: Co-fire the internal electrodes in a low-oxygen atmosphere
children.description: A multilayer capacitor's internal electrode is nickel or palladium, printed as a paste and co-fired with the ceramic. That will not work in air - the ceramic would reduce and become a lossy semiconductor - so the whole stack is fired in a low-oxygen atmosphere at 1200-1350 C in hydrogen or in a nitrogen-hydrogen mix, and then re-oxidised afterwards so the barium titanate goes back to being an insulator. The oxygen partial pressure is controlled to a few millibars. It is the most metallurgically demanding step in the whole electronics supply chain that nobody ever sees, and it is a barium carbonate problem.

facts.label: Electrode
facts.value: nickel or palladium paste, screen-printed

facts.label: Atmosphere
facts.value: low pO2, a few millibars, in H2 or N2/H2

facts.label: Reoxidation
facts.value: a separate anneal afterwards to restore the insulator

children.note: Medium confidence; the co-firing atmosphere is standard practice but the exact pO2 is proprietary.

metal.ammonium-phosphate.name: Ammonium phosphate (refined phosphate salt)
metal.ammonium-phosphate.description: Ammonium phosphate salts, chiefly diammonium phosphate (NH4)2HPO4 and monoammonium phosphate, made by reacting ammonia with wet-process phosphoric acid digested from phosphate rock; diammonium phosphate carries 18-46-0 NPK and is the dominant phosphate fertiliser. The same salts serve electronics manufacture: inorganic phosphates are among the most common anodic-oxidation electrolytes for aluminium capacitor foil, and ammonium phosphate and phosphite salts are compounded into capacitor electrolytes at fractions of a percent.

facts.label: DAP formula
facts.value: (NH4)2HPO4

facts.label: Capacitor electrolyte salt
facts.value: 0.2 wt% ammonium phosphate in a DMF/oxalic-acid electrolyte example (1982 capacitor patent)
